column1: # TITLE: Lung adenocarcinoma and mesothelioma DNA methylation
# SUMMARY: Pathologic differentiation of tissue of origin in tumors found in the lung can be challenging
column2: with differentiation of mesothelioma and lung adenocarcinoma emblematic of this problem. Indeed
column3: proper classification is essential for determination of treatment regimen for these diseases
column4: making accurate and early diagnosis critical. Here we investigate the potential of epigenetic profiles of lung adenocarcinoma
column6: and non-malignant pulmonary tissues (n=285) as differentiation markers in an analysis of DNA methylation at 1413 autosomal CpG loci associated with 773 cancer-related genes. Using an unsupervised recursively-partitioned mixture modeling technique for all samples
column7: the derived methylation profile classes were significantly associated with sample type (P < 0.0001). In a similar analysis restricted to tumors
column8: methylation profile classes significantly predicted tumor type (P < 0.0001). Random forests classification of CpG methylation of tumors - which splits the data into training and test sets - accurately differentiated MPM from lung adenocarcinoma over 99% of the time (P < 0.0001). In a locus-by-locus comparison of CpG methylation between tumor types
column9: 1266 CpG loci had significantly different methylation between tumors following correction for multiple comparisons (Q < 0.05); 61% had higher methylation in adenocarcinoma. Using the CpG loci with significant differential methylation in a pathways analysis revealed significant enrichment of methylated gene-loci in Cell Cycle Regulation
column12: and Apoptosis Signaling pathways in lung adenocarcinoma when compared to mesothelioma. Methylation-profile-based differentiation of lung adenocarcinoma and mesothelioma is highly accurate
column13: informs on the distinct etiologies of these diseases
column14: and holds promise for clinical application.
